correctness.rationale: The exact claim is for each real 1<p<∞ and a>b>0 on real/complex ell_p^4, all six arrangements of (a,a,b,b). Duality map is |x_j|^{p-2}conj(x_j) with its continuous zero extension. Positive phases attain the triangle inequality, giving max Φ=Σw_j s_j^α s_{j+1}^β over the 4-simplex, α=(p−1)/p and β=1/p. Concavity of weighted geometric mean is strict up to proportional pairs; connected cyclic edges and mass normalization give unique maximizing positive simplex vector; a zero mass can be improved by transfer from an adjacent positive mass of order epsilon^α or epsilon^β versus O(epsilon) losses. For alternating (a,b,a,b), 2-step cyclic symmetry forces masses s1=s3,s2=s4, yielding H(t)=(a t^{p−1}+bt)/(1+t^p) with unique t>0. Its derivative at t=1 is (p−2)(a−b)/4, hence t>1 for p>2, t<1 for p<2, t=1 for p=2. For grouped (a,a,b,b), evaluating x=(t,t,1,1) for p>2 and (t,1,1,t) for p<2 yields exactly respective positive gaps (t−1)(a t^{p−1}−b)/(2(1+t^p)) and (1−t^{p−1})(a−bt)/(2(1+t^p)); all positive because a>b and t crosses 1 in the proved direction. For p=2, symmetric bipartite matrix singular values give grouped sqrt((a²+b²)/2), alternating (a+b)/2, strict by (a−b)^2>0. Four adjacent vs two alternating placements exhaust all six rotations, and at a=b all radii agree. Every quantifier follows from this analytic argument, not the finite verifier.
residual_risks: Does not cover p=1, p=∞, nonpositive/complex weights, other multiplicities or longer cycles.
The claimed upper-free adjacent exact radius p≠2 is not supplied; the strict certificate alone suffices for the inequality.
72 numerical settings and random tests corroborate only finite examples; proof relies on fractional-power boundary argument and strict simplex concavity.

value.rationale: The smallest directed cycle with two inequivalent repeated-two-weight arrangement orbits naturally asks which placement maximizes the Banach spatial numerical radius. The theorem gives a complete global (not perturbative) extremal classification for every weight ratio and every smooth l_p exponent, and explicit nonzero gap witnesses whose forms differ across p=2. This is a motivated structural operator-norm/duality-map ordering rather than a narrow arbitrary table. Unlike earlier local Hessian, no small-contrast restriction remains. It stops at four sites and does not claim exact non-Hilbert grouped radius or a general cycle rearrangement theorem.
residual_risks: Contribution is specialized to four sites and multiplicity 2+2; significance does not extend automatically to arbitrary cycles.
The all-p strict inequality has short trial-vector proofs once uniqueness is established; this does not by itself erase its motivated sharp global classification, but limits generality.
